name: Plecanatide
route: One 3 mg tablet by mouth daily, with or without food
status: FDA-approved for adults: chronic idiopathic constipation (2017) and IBS with constipation (2018)
mechanism: Copies the gut hormone uroguanylin to switch on guanylate cyclase-C receptors in the small intestine, which pulls water into the bowel and softens stool
uses: Irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) in adults

article.summary: Plecanatide (Trulance) is a once-daily tablet that mimics the gut hormone uroguanylin. It is FDA-approved for chronic idiopathic constipation and IBS with constipation in adults.
article.takeaway: Plecanatide is a near copy of uroguanylin, a hormone the small intestine makes to control fluid in the gut. By switching on its receptor, it draws water into the bowel and makes stools easier to pass. In a 12-week trial in chronic constipation, **21% met a strict response goal versus 10% on placebo**.[^1] Diarrhea is the main side effect, affecting about 4-6% of people in trials.[^1][^2] It is approved only for adults and must not be used in children under 6.[^3]
glance: Chronic idiopathic constipation and IBS-C in adults
One 3 mg tablet daily; can be crushed into applesauce or water

blocks.text: Cells lining the small intestine release uroguanylin, a short peptide hormone that binds the guanylate cyclase-C (GC-C) receptor. That raises cyclic GMP inside the cells and opens a chloride channel called CFTR. Chloride and bicarbonate flow into the gut, water follows, and the stool becomes softer and moves faster.

Plecanatide is a 16-amino-acid peptide identical to uroguanylin except for one amino acid swap. Like the natural hormone, it binds best in the slightly acidic environment of the upper small intestine. It is barely absorbed, so it acts almost entirely inside the gut.

items: **Chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC):** long-term hard, infrequent or incomplete bowel movements without another cause
**IBS with constipation (IBS-C):** recurring belly pain linked to constipation

blocks.text: US gastroenterology guidelines give plecanatide a strong recommendation for chronic idiopathic constipation and a conditional one for IBS-C, where the evidence for [linaclotide](/peptides/linaclotide) is rated stronger.[^4][^5]

rows: Durable responders: 21.0% on 3 mg vs 10.2% on placebo; about 2.5 more complete bowel movements per week[^1]
Pain-plus-bowel responders: 30.2% vs 17.8% and 21.5% vs 14.2% on placebo[^2]

blocks.text: A 6 mg dose was also tested and worked no better than 3 mg, and the approved dose is 3 mg.[^1][^2] In a 2025 pooled analysis of 605 adults aged 18-40 with IBS-C and bloating, 23% improved in pain, bloating and bowel movements at the same time, versus 13% on placebo.[^6]

The dose for both conditions is one 3 mg tablet a day, with or without food. People who have trouble swallowing can crush the tablet and mix it with applesauce or water, and it can be given through a feeding tube following the label instructions.[^3]

items: **Diarrhea** is the most common side effect (about 4-6% in trials versus 1% on placebo), and only 1-2% stopped treatment because of it[^1][^2]
**Severe diarrhea:** stop the drug and get medical advice, because of the risk of dehydration
**Boxed warning:** contraindicated in children under 6 after young mice died of dehydration, and should be avoided from 6 to 17 years; it is not approved for anyone under 18[^3]
**Not for** people with a known or suspected bowel obstruction

evidence.label: Approved: several large phase 3 trials
evidence.text: Three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials with more than 3,500 adults support plecanatide.[^1][^2] As with most constipation drugs, the absolute gain over placebo is moderate, and long-term comparisons with other agents are limited.

faq.q: How does plecanatide compare with linaclotide?
faq.a: Both act on the same GC-C receptor and have similar results in trials. [Linaclotide](/peptides/linaclotide) comes in several doses and has pediatric approvals, while plecanatide has one adult dose. No large head-to-head trial has compared them.

faq.q: Can plecanatide be taken with food?
faq.a: Yes. Unlike some constipation medicines, it can be taken with or without a meal.[^3]
No. It is contraindicated under age 6 and should be avoided from 6 to 17 because of the risk of serious dehydration.[^3]
